headline: Auto lending growth and wider margin lift profit and returns
summary_short: Ally's Q3 2026 GAAP EPS was $1.30 (+10% y/y) and adjusted EPS $1.34 (+16% y/y), on pre-tax income of $567M and a 3.66% net interest margin ex. OID.
summary_long: Net income to common holders rose to $401M from $367M last quarter and $371M a year ago. Return on common equity was 12.1% and core ROTCE 13.1%. Consumer auto originations were $12.9B, up 10% y/y, on a record 4.8M applications. Retail auto net charge-offs were 189 bps, up 1 bp y/y. Retail deposits reached $142B. The common equity tier 1 ratio was 10.2%, the company repurchased $178M of shares and announced a $0.35 fourth-quarter dividend.
confidence_notes: Adjusted EPS, core ROTCE and NIM ex. OID are non-GAAP measures as defined by Ally. The shard EPS of 1.34 is the adjusted figure; GAAP EPS is $1.30.

drivers.explanation: The CEO says the focused strategy is delivering: core franchises are growing, returns are improving and credit discipline is being maintained.
Dealer Financial Services delivered record application volume and nearly $13B of originations, while Insurance posted a 36% ROE and Corporate Finance a 22% ROE.
The margin ex. OID rose 3 bps q/q and 11 bps y/y; the release does not break out the causes.
Capital strengthened while the company still executed $178M of repurchases in the quarter.
